precepts.text: In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes, and that includes taking heathen women.
precepts.point: Ruth clave to Naomi: thy people shall be my people and thy God my God; she is the picture of the ten men who will take hold of the skirt of a Jew and say, we will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Naomi told Ruth, “Behold, thy sister in law is gone back unto her people, and unto her gods”. Orpah went back to Moab, to her people and her gods. These were not Israelite women; this was a heathen woman of another nation. That is important, because there are doctrines out there teaching that Ruth was an Israelite. No, she was not. She was a heathen. Was it right for Boaz to deal with a heathen? No, but it happened.

Just in case there is any confusion, the last verse of Judges, right above Ruth, shows why it happened: “In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.” During the judges, we did what we wanted to do.

And Ruth opens in that very time: “Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled”. There was no king. It was the time when Israel did what they wanted, and that included taking heathen women.

So Ruth's story does not make her an Israelite, and it does not make it right to take a heathen wife. It shows what Israel was doing when every man did what was right in his own eyes. The scripture keeps calling her what she is: “Ruth the Moabitess”. That is clear.

precepts.text: If a man vow a vow unto the Lord or swear an oath, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth. This is the law Israel was bound by when they swore concerning their daughters.
precepts.point: The question of the chapter: how shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the Lord not to give them our daughters? They made a vow, they swore to the Lord, and the law says a sworn oath must be performed; that is why they could not simply turn around and give their daughters.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

precepts.why:
Here is the law Israel was bound by when they swore concerning their daughters. Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes, “This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded. If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.”

That is why the question of the whole chapter is what it is: “How shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the Lord that we will not give them of our daughters to wives?” They made a vow, they swore to the Lord, and a sworn oath must be performed. They could not simply turn around and give their daughters; whatever proceeded out of their mouth had to stand.

precepts.text: There was no king in Israel and every man did that which was right in his own eyes; that is the state Israel was in when these marriages happened.
precepts.point: Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No. But remember what was just read at the end of Judges: “In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.”

That is the state Israel was in when Mahlon and Chilion took Orpah and Ruth. There was no king to hold the nation to the law, and every man did what seemed right to himself.

precepts.text: The virgins of Jabeshgilead had not known man by lying with any male; to know somebody in scripture means to lie with them.
precepts.point: Naomi answered, Sit still, my daughter, until thou know how the matter will fall: for the man will not be in rest until he have finished the thing this day.

note.label: Ruth 3: The Skirt of the Near Kinsman

precepts.why:
Ruth lay at his feet until the morning, and rose up before one could know another. Knowing here is the same precept read in Judges 21. “And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh–gilead four hundred young virgins, that had known no man by lying with any male: and they brought them unto the camp to Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.”

The virgins had known no man by lying with any male; to know somebody in scripture means to lie with them, to have sex. So in this case, before one could know another means before they lay down together, and that is also why Boaz said, Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor.

moments.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

points: The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpeh that not one of them would give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife. This follows the previous chapter, where the tribes went to war against Benjamin.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The people came to the house of God and sat there till evening before God, lifted up their voices and wept sore, asking why it had come to pass that there should be one tribe lacking in Israel. The next day they rose early, built an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their brother, for there was one tribe cut off from Israel that day. They had also made a great oath that whoever came not up to the Lord at Mizpeh would surely be put to death.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The question of the chapter: how shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the Lord not to give them our daughters? They made a vow, they swore to the Lord, and the law says a sworn oath must be performed; that is why they could not simply turn around and give their daughters.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: They searched which tribe came not up to Mizpeh, and behold, none had come from Jabeshgilead to the assembly. So under the great oath the congregation sent twelve thousand of the valiantest men to smite Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, destroying every male and every woman that had lain by man.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: Among the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead they found four hundred young virgins that had not known man by lying with any male, and brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The whole congregation sent to speak peaceably to the children of Benjamin at the rock Rimmon, and Benjamin came again. They gave them the wives saved alive of the women of Jabeshgilead, but they sufficed not; there were not enough for all the men that remained.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The people repented them for Benjamin because the Lord had made a breach in the tribes of Israel, and the elders said there must be an inheritance for them that be escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: Verse 18 restates why they could not just give their own daughters: the children of Israel had sworn, saying, Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin. That is the same oath read in verse 7.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The solution: there was a yearly feast of the Lord in Shiloh, so they commanded the children of Benjamin to lie in wait in the vineyards, and when the daughters of Shiloh came out to dance in the dances, every man was to catch him a wife of the daughters of Shiloh and go to the land of Benjamin.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: When the fathers or brethren came to complain, the elders would answer, Be favourable unto them for our sakes; because the fathers did not give their daughters, they would not be guilty of breaking the oath.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The children of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number of them that danced, then returned to their inheritance, repaired the cities, and dwelt in them.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The children of Israel departed thence at that time, every man to his tribe, to his family, and to his inheritance.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin
